title: Poor User Experience with Car Insurance!
text:
I was trying to purchase car insurance through PhonePe, but the experience was quite disappointing. When selecting an insurance plan, the app simply displays a list of insurance providers and their prices without providing any meaningful details about policy benefits, coverage, exclusions or features.

How is a customer supposed to compare insurers and make an informed decision without knowing what each policy actually offers?

Even basic information like coverage details, personal accident benefits, third-party liability limits and policy exclusions should be readily available before asking customers to proceed with their details.

Insurance is an important financial decision, not an impulse purchase. Customers should be able to understand and compare policies before committing to one.

Please improve this experience by providing a proper View Benefits / Compare Policies option for every insurer.

A customer-first experience should educate customers before asking them to buy.

title: Respect User Choices! Stop Forcing Push Notifications
text:
I have been using PhonePe for many years, but I am now seriously disappointed with the app’s repeated attempts to force me to enable push notifications.

Every time I use the app, I am confronted with pop-ups asking me to allow notifications. This constant nagging is frustrating and completely unnecessary. If I wanted notifications, I would enable them myself. And once enabled, users risk being flooded with unnecessary notifications.

When a user says NO, it means NO! A user’s decision should be respected instead of repeatedly pressuring them to change it.

An app that prioritizes its own engagement strategy over user preferences eventually loses user trust. After years of using PhonePe, I have decided to uninstall it and switch to alternatives that respect my choices and provide a less intrusive experience.

PhonePe, please learn to respect your users’ decisions. A good user experience is about giving people control, not repeatedly forcing them to reconsider their choices.

title: Poor App Fluidity and Performance on iPhone 17 Pro Max
text:
I am using an iPhone 17 Pro Max, and my biggest issue with Google Pay is its poor scrolling and overall app fluidity. The app feels like it is running at just 60Hz or even below, with noticeable lack of smoothness.

When I use PhonePe, the experience is completely different. PhonePe feels extremely smooth and responsive. Google Pay, on the other hand, feels like an app running on an older, low-RAM smartphone.

To be clear, this is not an issue with my iPhone. All my other apps work perfectly smoothly, including PhonePe. I have also tried uninstalling and reinstalling Google Pay, but the issue remains.

Interestingly, I experience the exact same issue on my wife’s iPhone 14 Pro Max as well. This clearly seems to be an app-level performance issue rather than a device-specific problem.

Google Pay seriously needs to improve its UI fluidity, scrolling performance, and overall responsiveness.

After this experience, I have decided to permanently switch to PhonePe for my UPI transactions.

The GPay app, clearly hasn’t been built or tested by anyone living in India or using payments on a daily basis and it shows. The app tries initiating random sms tries to the NPCI endpoints to activate my previously active bank accounts and UPI IDs on a DUAL-SIM device and of course, ends up failing and hitting the daily sms limit for activations 🫠

Now, I’m flying out in under 12 hours, sure, you can blame me for trying this last minute, but . . I expect Google written software to . . Work? Is that too much of an expectation? Customer support didn’t even know that the App sends out SMSes through the system interface so wasn’t of any help here at all. I tried so hard to the point of sheer frustration.

Anyway, searched for the competition, and turns out PhonePe has the largest share in the market (surprise to me) so I try their app. I kid you not, I’m up and running with FIVE new UPI IDs in under a minute!! I have the timestamps from when I got the first verification sms while signing in to when all UPI IDs were active and I got the email notification saying so. 🫠🫠🫠

title: Frequent payment issues
text:
I have been using Google Pay for years, but my experience with UPI payment failures has been disappointing. This is not the first time this has happened. I have faced similar issues a few times over the past several years.

Recently, I paid ₹500 for an Uber ride through Google Pay. The amount was debited from my bank account, but the driver was informed that the payment had failed. As a result, I had to pay ₹500 in cash. Later, the original UPI payment was also credited to the driver, resulting in a duplicate payment.

Uber refunded me ₹500 as a goodwill gesture. However, Google Pay support only explained that such delays can occur due to communication issues between banks and the UPI network. They advised me to wait for the final transaction status before making another payment.

My concern is simple: what should a customer do when immediate payment is required and the recipient claims they have not received the money? What happens if the amount involved is ₹10,000 or ₹50,000 instead of ₹500?

A payment app should not only facilitate transactions but also provide effective customer support and clear solutions when things go wrong. I expected a proper investigation and guidance on how customers can recover duplicate payments, rather than just a technical explanation.

Google Pay is convenient when everything works, but recurring payment issues and inadequate grievance redressal are serious concerns. Customers should not have to depend on the goodwill of a merchant or service provider to recover their money.

I hope Google Pay takes these issues seriously and improves its payment reliability and customer protection mechanisms.

title: Incorrect User Names and Bank Account Linking
text:
I have encountered this issue twice, and I would like to report it again because it appears to be a serious bug in Google Pay.
Issue 1: Multiple Names Showing for the Same Phone Number
When someone enters my phone number to send me money, Google Pay displays multiple users with different names associated with the same phone number. My name is also displayed along with other people's names, even though the phone number is the same. This creates confusion about which user is the actual recipient.
Issue 2: Money Transfers Possible Without a Bank Account Linked to My Number
I do not have any bank account in my name linked to my phone number, and I have never opened a bank account using that number. However, when someone enters my phone number in Google Pay from another person's phone, my number still appears as a valid recipient, and money can be transferred to it.
My Concern:
How can multiple users with different names be associated with the same phone number? And how is it possible to receive money through Google Pay using my phone number when I do not have any bank account linked to it?
I request the Google Pay team to investigate these issues, check the phone number and bank account mapping, and resolve this bug as soon as possible. This issue raises serious concerns about incorrect recipient identification and the safety of money transfers.
Please take this report seriously and provide a proper explanation and solution.

While migrating from old phone to new the mandates were revoked temporarily. Now after actuvating they all look generically pointing to Axis Bank. There is no way to resolve this as it has to feature restart the mandate with original biller name shown. 

 This is a frustrating visual bug and synchronization conflict caused by how the NPCI BHIM App and Axis Bank are communicating the metadata of your reactivated mandates.
When you reactivated the mandate, BHIM pulled the technical "UMRN" (Unique Mandate Reference Number) or the financing bank's name (Axis Bank) instead of the merchant tag (like the utility or phone provider). Because the backend server still considers those invisible mandates active under your phone number/account, it blocks you from creating a new one with a "mandate already exists" error.

title: Feedback and Suggestions for Improvement – SBI YONO Application
text:
Dear SBI Team,

I would like to share my feedback regarding the SBI YONO application and highlight a few issues that need attention.

Currently, the application does not appear to be properly optimised. I have experienced the following problems:

1. Slow Loading: The application takes too much time to load, which affects the overall user experience.
2. SSA Account Not Visible: My SSA (Sukanya Samriddhi Account) is not available for viewing in the YONO application.
3. Convert to Salary Account Option Not Working: The option to convert an account into a Salary Account does not seem to function properly.
4. Account Summary Improvements: The YONO Lite application provides a better account-viewing experience, with all accounts accessible under Account Summary. I would appreciate similar functionality in the main YONO application.

My Suggestions:

• Optimise the YONO application to improve loading speed and overall performance.
• Enable SSA account viewing and balance details in the application.
• Fix the bugs affecting the Convert to Salary Account option.
• Provide a unified Account Summary displaying all linked SBI accounts, including SSA accounts.
• Improve the application’s stability and overall user experience.

At present, I am using YONO Lite because it offers a more convenient account-viewing experience.

I request SBI to address these issues and make the main YONO application more user-friendly, efficient and feature-complete.

I hope the SBI technical team will consider this feedback and take the necessary steps in upcoming updates.

Thank you.

YONO SBI 2.0 is a welcome initiative by the State Bank of India towards improving its digital banking services. The application brings various banking facilities under one platform, making it convenient for customers to access their accounts and perform routine banking transactions without visiting a branch.

The redesigned interface and availability of multiple services provide a more comprehensive banking experience. Facilities such as balance enquiry, account statements, fund transfers, UPI payments, fixed deposits and digital loan services make everyday banking easier and more accessible.

However, as a customer, I feel that there is still considerable scope for improvement. The application should be faster and more responsive, particularly while logging in, checking account balances and performing transactions. Navigation should be further simplified so that commonly used services can be accessed without going through multiple screens.

Transaction processing should be smooth and reliable, with clear and immediate confirmation of successful, failed or pending transactions. The application should also provide better error messages instead of displaying generic technical errors, which often leave customers confused.

Customer support and grievance redressal should be more effectively integrated into the application. Customers should be able to register complaints, track their status and receive timely updates without having to visit a branch.

Overall, YONO SBI 2.0 has the potential to become a comprehensive digital banking solution. SBI deserves recognition for continuously upgrading its digital banking platform. However, the real success of the application will depend on its speed, stability, ease of use and ability to provide a seamless banking experience.

My expectation is that SBI will continue to improve the application based on customer feedback and make it more user-friendly, reliable and efficient
